subject: Urban Planning
subcategory: Parks, Green Spaces, and Public Land
title: Urban Forests: Trees as Infrastructure
description: A 60-second lesson on Urban Forests: Trees as Infrastructure.

hook.text: A single mature tree provides $300 worth of cooling, pollution filtering, and stormwater capture per year.

buildup.text: Urban forests are not random plantings. They're planned canopy networks with species selected for each street.

discovery.text: Trees reduce air conditioning costs, increase property values, and lower crime rates in surrounding blocks.

twist.text: Low-income neighborhoods have 25% less tree canopy than wealthy ones. Tree planting follows money, not need.

climax.text: Los Angeles pledged to plant 90,000 trees in underserved neighborhoods by 2028. Shade as reparation.

punchline.text: Trees are the cheapest infrastructure a city can build.

quiz.question: How much less tree canopy do low-income neighborhoods typically have?
